key_insight: A cross-validated DNS–PIV dataset captures turbulent wakes behind nine bluff-body geometries at Re = 10,000, enabling comparisons across distinct separation behaviors.
engineering_relevance: The dataset supports development and testing of data-driven turbulence closures, reduced-order models, and wake-stability analyses across geometries.
method: Wall-resolved spectral-element DNS for nine bluff-body shapes and orientations.
Time-resolved planar PIV in the MIT Intelligent Towing Tank.
Matched mean fields and 24-bin phase averages keyed to the lift signal.
evidence_signal: The DNS setup is verified against reference cylinder data at Re = 3900, and DNS and PIV fields are compared at Re = 10,000.
watch_item: The dataset targets Re = 10,000 and provides only one instantaneous 3D DNS snapshot per body, limiting assessment of generalization and time-resolved 3D dynamics.
paper_title: Turbulent wakes behind nine bluff-body shapes from direct numerical simulation and particle image velocimetry
